person: a cousin you grew up with
shape: a younger self and an older self, one small moment apart

slides.text: we spent every holiday sharing [[the thin pull-out couch]] in grandma's back room.
you always claimed the side with the metal bar, so i could sleep near the window.
we giggled about the grown-ups in the kitchen until we heard grandma's slippers in the hall.
but we grew up, and we only saw each other at the big family events.
we stood in the church hall yesterday, balancing dry cake on paper plates.
you caught my eye across the crowd, walked past three aunts, and didn't ask any polite questions.
you just sat on the low brick planter by the door, leaving exactly half the space for me.
[[we don't fit on one couch anymore]], but you still take the side with the bar.

caption:
some people never let you stand alone in a crowded room.
send this to the cousin who always sat next to you at the kids' table.
alt: A series of slides featuring a small green donkey telling a story about growing up with a cousin, starting from sharing a thin pull-out couch at grandma's house to finding a quiet place to sit together at a crowded family event years later.
hook_options: we spent every holiday sharing the thin pull-out couch in grandma's back room.
we spent every summer holiday sharing one rusted bike in grandma's backyard.
we used to sit on the kitchen counter and split one soda with two straws.
